tasks.short: Maintain customer relationships and resolve payment, billing, and financial service problems.

steps.what: Check customer balances, invoices, and payment terms in the {ERP}.
Read the customer complaint and correspondence in the {EMAIL}.

loop.input: Selected customer correspondence, complaint, and account summary.
loop.output: Issue brief with requests, disputed facts, deadlines, and source references.
loop.check: Require source references; verify amounts against the account summary; flag conflicting statements.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per case; unresolved conflicts return to manual reading.
loop.why_not_simpler: Customer requests and explanations arrive as free text with inconsistent wording.

steps.what: Discuss the problem, understand constraints, and rebuild trust with the customer.
Decide a settlement or payment arrangement within delegated authority.
Draft the agreed explanation, terms, and next steps in the {EMAIL}.

loop.input: Approved resolution decision and discussion notes.
loop.output: Customer reply draft stating approved terms and next steps.
loop.check: Compare amounts, dates, and commitments with the resolution decision; flag unsupported promises.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; failed checks return to manual drafting.
loop.why_not_simpler: The explanation must address the customer's specific concerns in natural language.

steps.what: Approve and send the customer reply through the {EMAIL}.
Record the outcome and follow-up date in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: An integration retrieves the account summary from the {ERP}; bounded loops turn selected {EMAIL} correspondence into a sourced issue brief and reply draft. The finance manager conducts the conversation and authorises commitments before sending, while configured {CRM} workflows record the outcome and follow-up.
tasks.previous_blocker: Account facts and correspondence are separated. Relationship repair and settlement decisions require personal judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing interfaces support account retrieval and activity logging. AI-assisted coding can reduce integration effort, and bounded loops can prepare sourced summaries.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed facts, unusual contracts, and distressed customers need attention. Larger concessions require escalation under the approval policy.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising unspoken concerns, rebuilding trust, and choosing a commercially fair resolution.

ambition.what: Early payment-difficulty conversations for smaller business customers.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less account reconstruction and more customer problem solving. Settlement authority remains defined by the existing delegation.

reach.task: Arrange realistic payment plans for overdue accounts.
reach.learn: Learn collection stages, affordability questions, and escalation thresholds.

reach.task: Assess whether revised payment terms increase credit exposure.
reach.learn: Learn credit-limit logic and how disputed invoices affect exposure.

evidence.claim: Account retrieval, approved correspondence, and activity logging can use deterministic integrations and configured workflows.
Free-text summaries and replies need source checks and human review before customer commitments.

assumptions: This task concerns corporate customer accounts and disputes rather than regulated investment advice.
The company uses the {CRM} for customer activity and the {ERP} for account balances.
Time shares are estimates of task effort, with relationship work remaining dominant.
Build ranges estimate a limited pilot; access and any consultation under national rules can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which customer records and correspondence the finance manager may access.
Whether the {ERP} and {CRM} expose suitable interfaces.
Whether national rules require employee consultation for the proposed processing.
research_questions: Do issue briefs preserve disputed facts and customer intent?
Can existing {CRM} configuration capture approved correspondence without custom code?
new_work: Review issue briefs and reply drafts.
Resolve conflicting records and failed account matches.
Maintain templates, access permissions, and integration mappings.

tasks.short: Monitor liquidity, forecast cash needs, and oversee authorised movements of funds.

steps.what: Check balances and recent movements in the {BANK}.
Check receivables, payables, and planned disbursements in the {ERP}.
Reconcile balances and expected movements in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Update the cash forecast and scenarios in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Decide funding, payment priorities, and transfers against liquidity limits.
Prepare payment or transfer instructions in the {BANK}.
Check and authorise release of instructions in the {BANK}.

tasks.design: Scheduled integrations bring {BANK} and {ERP} data into the {DATA_PLATFORM}, where deterministic reconciliation and scenario calculations feed a {BI} liquidity dashboard. The finance manager chooses cash actions, and configured {BANK} controls require authorised signatories before funds move.
tasks.previous_blocker: Bank formats, forecast assumptions, and payment calendars differ. Reliable reconciliation and secure access cost more than the forecast calculation itself.
tasks.enabler_now: Bank feeds, finance exports, and existing approval controls support a practical build. AI-assisted coding can accelerate adapters and validation rules without replacing treasury judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Receipt timing, restricted cash, currency exposure, and sudden funding needs remain uncertain. Payment release requires strong segregation of duties.
tasks.human_edge: Balancing liquidity resilience, supplier relationships, financing costs, and commercial priorities.

ambition.what: A daily downside-liquidity review using delayed-receipt scenarios.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling cash positions to challenging assumptions and choosing responses earlier. No new payment authority is granted by the automation.

reach.task: Manage short-term funding and liquidity buffers.
reach.learn: Learn funding lead times, covenant headroom, and treasury controls.

reach.task: Assess liquidity under adverse receipt and currency scenarios.
reach.learn: Learn stress assumptions and exposure limits.

evidence.claim: Nomentia supports cash forecasting using bank and finance data and forecast-versus-actual comparison.
Reconciliation, scenario arithmetic, and approval routing can be deterministic; funding decisions retain human judgement.

assumptions: The task concerns corporate treasury rather than securities trading or fund management.
A spreadsheet currently joins bank positions, expected movements, and forecast assumptions.
Time shares represent the end-to-end oversight task, including treasury support and signatory checks.
Build ranges are pilot estimates, not measured delivery results.
unknowns: Bank feed availability, security requirements, and charges.
Whether existing software already provides suitable forecasting.
Currencies, accounts, cash restrictions, and intercompany arrangements.
Signatory rules and whether the finance manager is an authorised signatory.
Access lead times and any applicable consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which reconciliation exceptions require judgement rather than better matching rules?
Would configuring existing forecasting be cheaper than building the proposed calculations?
new_work: Resolve stale feeds and unmatched cash movements.
Maintain receipt assumptions, scenario parameters, and liquidity limits.
Monitor access controls and retain approval evidence.

tasks.short: Direct finance-team workloads, resolve operational priorities, and coach employees.

steps.what: Review overdue finance work and control exceptions in the {ERP}.
Prepare a team capacity and deadline plan in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Choose priorities, responsibilities, and escalation routes in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Discuss dependencies, obstacles, and responsibilities with the finance team.
Coach individual employees on difficult work and development needs.
Record agreed owners, dates, and escalations in the {PROJECT}.

tasks.design: Configured {ERP} reports expose overdue work and control exceptions; deterministic calculations create a team capacity plan from deadlines and declared availability. The finance manager assigns people and handles coaching, while configured {PROJECT} workflows record approved assignments and send reminders.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finance queues and team planning are separate. Informal dependencies and personal circumstances make fully automatic assignment unsuitable.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting and work-management configuration can handle much of the task. Small integrations and capacity calculations are easier to build and maintain with AI-assisted coding.
tasks.still_hard: Skill coverage, segregation of duties, development needs, and competing deadlines require judgement. Employee-data processing needs GDPR assessment and consultation where national rules apply; later AI-based allocation would also need EU AI Act assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Understanding capability and motivation, handling conflict, and developing people while protecting financial controls.

ambition.what: A weekly close-capacity decision before deadline pressure becomes overtime.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less status collection and more coaching and early capacity decisions. The manager retains existing assignment rights; staffing and pay changes still need their established approvals.

reach.task: Compare temporary staffing costs with the cost of delayed finance work.
reach.learn: Learn capacity-cost scenarios and budget approval limits.

reach.task: Define useful process backlog and deadline metrics.
reach.learn: Learn metric definitions, refresh checks, and misleading workload proxies.

evidence.claim: Deadline arithmetic, team capacity summaries, approved assignment recording, and reminders can use deterministic technology.
Process workload measures cannot alone determine individual capability, development needs, or fair assignments.

assumptions: The finance manager leads a corporate finance team rather than a financial-services branch.
A spreadsheet currently bridges operational reporting and team planning.
Capacity calculations use declared availability and process demand; the manager assigns individual employees.
Build ranges estimate a pilot; national consultation processes may take longer.
unknowns: Which queues, deadlines, and assignments are already available in existing systems.
Team size, skill coverage, and segregation-of-duties requirements.
Whether recording availability introduces new employee-data processing.
Applicable national consultation requirements and existing employee agreements.
research_questions: Can configured reports replace manual status collection without new monitoring?
Which capacity measures predict bottlenecks without becoming individual performance scores?
new_work: Maintain task dependencies, capacity assumptions, and control constraints.
Correct missing queue records and stale availability.
Review access permissions and whether metrics create unintended incentives.

tasks.short: Define finance vacancies, assess candidates, and coordinate hiring with recruitment and human resources.

steps.what: Define responsibilities, essential criteria, and the role brief in the {DOCS}.
Approve the vacancy scope and funding through the {WORKFLOW}.
Create and publish the approved vacancy through the {ATS}.
Review applications against essential criteria in the {ATS}.
Arrange interviews using the {CALENDAR}.
Interview candidates and discuss relevant work examples.
Record the hiring decision and reasons in the {ATS}.
Prepare the offer from approved templates in the {DOCS}.
Approve terms and issue the offer through the {ESIGN}.

tasks.design: Approved role templates in the {DOCS} feed vacancy approval in the {WORKFLOW} and publication in the {ATS}. Configured {CALENDAR} scheduling and offer generation remove coordination work, while people assess candidates and approve offers before release through the {ESIGN}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Role definitions, vacancy approvals, scheduling, and offer paperwork cross several teams. Existing features may be only partly configured.
tasks.enabler_now: Templates, approval routing, scheduling, and document merging are established capabilities. AI-assisted coding can make small gaps between systems cheaper to close.
tasks.still_hard: Assessing evidence fairly, agreeing requirements, and attracting candidates remain human work. GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; any later AI candidate scoring needs separate assessment, and national rules may require consultation.
tasks.human_edge: Testing finance judgement, understanding motivation, and making a defensible hiring decision through direct interaction.

ambition.what: Career changers assessed through finance work examples and transferable skills.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time arranging interviews and assembling documents, with more time for candidate assessment. Hiring and pay approval rights follow the existing delegation.

reach.task: Design realistic work examples for assessing accounting and control judgement.
reach.learn: Learn which examples reveal competence and how to score evidence consistently.

reach.task: Review recruitment records and the proposed use of candidate data.
reach.learn: Learn retention limits, meaningful human review, and applicable national requirements.

evidence.claim: Vacancy approvals, scheduling, offer templates, and signature routing can largely use existing software configuration.
Candidate assessment and selection require meaningful human judgement in this design.

assumptions: The finance manager acts as hiring manager, supported by recruitment and human resources.
The company has approved role and offer templates and uses the listed system slots.
Scheduling uses approved shortlists and agreed availability.
The design introduces no automated candidate ranking or rejection.
Build ranges estimate a pilot; consultation and access waits may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Existing scheduling, document-generation, and approval capabilities.
Who approves vacancies, offers, and exceptions to pay bands.
Candidate-data retention rules and access permissions.
Whether work-example assessment is suitable for the roles being recruited.
research_questions: Which administrative features can be enabled without custom integration?
Do essential criteria exclude career changers without a clear job-related reason?
Can interview evidence support consistent selection reasons across candidates?
new_work: Maintain role criteria, interview guides, and offer templates.
Handle scheduling exceptions and failed signature routing.
Review permissions, retention settings, and selection records.

role.altitude: The finance manager spends less time reconstructing records and coordinating paperwork, and more time on liquidity choices, customer resolutions, coaching, and hiring. Better visibility supports earlier decisions; additional financial or employment authority requires explicit delegation.
reach: Treasurers and Controllers: short-term funding and liquidity buffers.
Credit Analysts: customer exposure and payment-term decisions.
Budget Analysts: capacity and staffing-cost scenarios.
Business Intelligence Analysts: reliable process metrics.
Compliance Officers: financial controls and personal-data use.
skills_to_grow: Define reconciliation rules and useful exception thresholds.
Challenge cash assumptions and interpret stress scenarios.
Review sourced summaries and detect unsupported commitments.
Design fair work examples and record hiring evidence.
Understand access controls, GDPR, the EU AI Act, and applicable national consultation rules.
role.ambitious_version: Run an early-warning finance service that connects liquidity stress, customer payment difficulties, and team bottlenecks to timely human decisions.
